block.name: search_rows_sql
block.title: Select rows using custom SQL
block.description: Select rows using custom SQL in SQL Server

input.sql:
SELECT tc.ASSIGNMENT_ID, tc.id as TIME_CARD_ID, tc.WEEK_ENDING, tl.PAYROLL_PROC_DATE, TIME_LINE_ID, tc.PAYMENT_METHOD, te.PAY_CODE, te.PAY_UNITS, te.PAY_RATE, te.BILL_CODE, te.BILL_UNITS, te.BILL_RATE, a.EMPLOYEE_ID, a.BRANCH_ID, a.CUSTOMER_NAME, tc.PAY_CYCLE, a.WEEK_ENDING_DAY, tc.CREATED_AT, tc.CREATED_BY, tc.MODIFIED_AT, tc.MODIFIED_BY

FROM TIME_ENTRY te

LEFT JOIN TIME_LINE tl on te.TIME_LINE_ID = tl.ID 

LEFT JOIN TIME_CARD tc on tl.TIME_CARD_ID = tc.ID

LEFT JOIN ASSIGNMENT a on tc.ASSIGNMENT_ID = a.NUMBER

WHERE tc.DELETED <> 1 AND tc.WEEK_ENDING BETWEEN :startDate AND :endDate
and tc.ASSIGNMENT_ID is not null

extended_input_schema.hint: First provide the full name assigned to your bind variable in the WHERE condition. e.g. id Second, provide the actual parameter value. Parameter values can be static or datapills. Select the closest corresponding data type that your database is expecting for the bind variable
